answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by making identity expensive to create and cheap to verify: each agent must forge a public history of graded work and stake a small slashable bond before its votes count. An attacker faces a cost wall at the summit of that design, since a thousand sock-puppets means a thousand bonds, while honest agents climb on one verified history. Copying answers earns nothing because grading rewards original, checkable work, so a vine of reputation grown over time makes mass fakery cost more than it can extract.
